summary: The article argues that redundant systems (backup power, alternative data channels, secondary networks) are essential to preventing major telecom disruptions, using a series of outages and successful failovers from September to November 2023 as examples. It weighs the cost and complexity of redundancy against the economic losses from outages, and stresses staff training, new technology, and global standards. It concludes that the goal is to minimize outage impact rather than eliminate outages entirely.
one_line: Redundant systems limit the impact of telecom outages, as shown by several 2023 US incidents, despite implementation costs and complexity.
key_facts: On November 9th, 2023, thousands of users across New York lost mobile service for several hours.
The New York mobile service interruption is estimated to have cost local businesses upwards of $15 million.
On September 15th, 2023, a major ISP in Atlanta suffered an outage when a construction mishap severed underground cables.
On October 6th, 2023, a software glitch caused network failure for a top-tier mobile operator in Chicago, affecting voice and data services for millions.
On October 24th, 2023, a leading telecom operator in Miami rerouted traffic through secondary networks within minutes of an unforeseen system outage.
On November 2nd, 2023, a regional ISP in San Francisco had an equipment failure, but its redundant systems kicked in flawlessly, with no noticeable service disruption.
Telecommunications analyst Sandra Kinnear said, "The technical and logistical aspects of creating redundant systems can be daunting."
Telecom consultant James Lipton called redundancy "an investment in reliability" when weighed against the potential fallout of a major outage.
Redundancy in telecom can mean backup power sources, alternative data channels, or entire networks that handle traffic if the main network fails.
Staff training, awareness workshops and regular drills help ensure redundant systems work when needed, as seen in the quick Miami resolution.
Cloud technology, AI-based monitoring, predictive analytics, modular data centers and portable network units are advancing redundancy.
The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) works on guidelines to help build more resilient telecom infrastructures globally.
The article says the goal is not to prevent outages entirely, which is nearly impossible, but to reduce their impact to the minimum.
